platform:ana.reflection2: My grade. It leaves out effort.

match.label: Matches its sheet
match.phrase: Reported the number its definition gives

off.label: Off its sheet
off.phrase: Reported a number its definition does not give

none.label: No number reported
none.phrase: The clock ran out before a number was locked

reviewQuestions: Which line of your definition decided your number, and who would want it written that way?
Name a number you are judged by. What is its definition, and what does it leave out?
lessonQuestions: What did your definition count, and what did it leave out?
If someone challenged your number, what would you show them first?
Who in the company would want retention measured your way?
What would change your number without changing the data?

lessons.head: A number is a definition, a measurement and a purpose.
lessons.text: The data was the same for every team. The definition and the purpose behind it set the number.

lessons.head: Every definition gives a correct number.
lessons.text: Each one answers its own question. None of them is the retention figure.

lessons.head: Ask for the definition before you argue about the number.
lessons.text: Two careful teams can defend two numbers far apart, and both can be correct.

lessons.head: Who writes the definition decides what counts.
lessons.text: Sales, Finance and Investor Relations each wrote the line that suits their job.

lines: Period: 1 July to 30 September.
Scope: only accounts active on 1 July. Accounts that signed up after 1 July are excluded.
Source: the account records in the data pack.
An account counts as retained if it was active on the last day of the quarter.
Report retention as a percentage to one decimal place, rounded half up.
A.purpose: Wins back a customer and wants credit for it.
derivation: 3 mid-quarter signups excluded; 40 accounts in scope.
4 accounts not retained: cancelled and still gone on the last day.

lines: Period: 1 July to 30 September.
Scope: only accounts active on 1 July. Accounts that signed up after 1 July are excluded.
Source: the account records in the data pack.
Retention is the share of starting monthly revenue still billed on the last day of the quarter, including accounts whose invoice is unpaid.
Report retention as a percentage to one decimal place, rounded half up.
derivation: 3 mid-quarter signups excluded; 40 accounts in scope, starting MRR $10,800.
4 cancelled accounts bill nothing at quarter end: -$2,126.

lines: Period: 1 July to 30 September.
Scope: only accounts active on 1 July. Accounts that signed up after 1 July are excluded.
Source: the account records in the data pack.
An account counts as retained if it was active on the last day of the quarter and had paid its quarter-end invoice.
Report retention as a percentage to one decimal place, rounded half up.
D.purpose: Unpaid isn't retained until the cash arrives.
derivation: 3 mid-quarter signups excluded; 40 accounts in scope.
10 accounts not retained: gone, or active with an unpaid quarter-end invoice.

lines: Period: 1 July to 30 September.
Scope: only accounts active on 1 July. Accounts that signed up after 1 July are excluded.
Source: the account records in the data pack.
An account counts as retained if it was active on the last day of the quarter on the same tier or higher.
Report retention as a percentage to one decimal place, rounded half up.
C.purpose: A downgrade means the product disappointed.
derivation: 3 mid-quarter signups excluded; 40 accounts in scope.
8 accounts not retained: gone, or on a lower tier than they started.

lines: Period: 1 July to 30 September.
Scope: only accounts active on 1 July. Accounts that signed up after 1 July are excluded.
Source: the account records in the data pack.
An account counts as retained if it was active on every day of the quarter.
Report retention as a percentage to one decimal place, rounded half up.
B.purpose: Any lapse means the relationship failed.
derivation: 3 mid-quarter signups excluded; 40 accounts in scope.
6 accounts not retained: cancelled at some point, including the two that came back.
